solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep only the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the word it follows

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time, like a second
first and third letters of base

explanation.surface: A baseball runner stumbles while reaching second base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on second base' reads as a baseball scene, but 'Falls on' is the definition and the rest builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mob someone is to crowd round and attack them, so it means to fall on or set upon.

clue.text: Crikey—I turned up late for work

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the short word is read from the bottom upward, so backwards

blocks.note: 'Man!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Crikey!'
taken as written
taken as written, then read upwards
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in dismay at having arrived late to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived', but it flips UP to PU in MAN + I + PU + LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To work clay or dough is to handle and shape it, which is to manipulate it.

blocks.note: Bootle is a town just north of Liverpool in Merseyside
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A town near Liverpool is said to be a good place for a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: Bootle is a town in Merseyside, the county around Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg describes illicitly copied goods, just as pirate does, as in a pirate recording.

clue.text: He'll represent people if he's given a different case

definitions.text: He'll represent people if he's given a different case

blocks.clueFragment: He'll represent people if he's given a different case
blocks.note: surface reading: a lawyer, who speaks for clients when handed a legal case to argue
setter's reading: this envoy represents a whole people, his nation, and the case he carries is the diplomatic bag

explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a barrister taking on a brief; the twist is that 'people' means a nation and 'case' is a diplomat's sealed bag rather than a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat posted abroad acts as the official representative of his country and its population.

indicators.note: something beset by another is surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
mange is a skin disease of animals

explanation.surface: Authorities struggle to contain a region stricken by an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN(A)GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage something is to run it or keep it in hand, a synonym of control as a verb.

blocks.note: a means one
pert means cheeky or fresh
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A single new bloom has just opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword river: something that flows. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, so it is an opening in the noun sense.

clue.text: Sat around piano on one new game show on TV

indicators.note: around says the first word's letters go round the next piece
new suggests the word that follows is made over into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: sat, as in seated, is sitting
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
Roman numeral one
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sat at a piano for a new TV game show.
explanation.walkthrough: S(P)ITTING + I + MAGE. Spitting Image was a British satirical TV show of the 1980s and 90s using latex puppets of politicians and celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a long-running ITV comedy programme, so it is a particular show on television.

indicators.note: off means the named letter is taken away from the word
something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A rifle shot has killed a well-groomed husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle shot' reads as a gunshot; really 'Rifle' is the verb defined and 'shot' rearranges what remains of the next word once its H is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack and plunder it, which is to despoil it.

clue.text: Hum when tough vocabulary's no good

indicators.note: no good tells us to remove the abbreviation for good from the word

blocks.note: language you cannot understand is 'all Greek to me'
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone mumbles when faced with difficult words they cannot use well.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum looks like a verb about singing, but in British slang a hum is a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Hum is British slang for a stink, so it is a synonym of reek as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Don't get me wrong number for criminal

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
a criminal act is an offence

explanation.surface: A prisoner protests to the guard about being known only by a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are said to soften a remark and assure the listener that no insult is intended.

blocks.note: a fair is a show or exhibition
and means also, in addition
square means dull and conventional

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on an event: merely a display, and a tedious one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely', but it is the adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fair and square is honest and above board, which is what just means as an adjective.

blocks.note: first meaning: to flow or come out
second meaning: one number of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a seasonal edition of a magazine; 'Spring' is the verb meaning to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for emerging or flowing out and a noun for one published number of a periodical.

clue.text: At times school may be one good way into worker's job

definitions.text: At times school may be one

indicators.note: into says the first pieces are placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the worker is a worker bee, whose job is carrying pollen between flowers

explanation.surface: A school may be a good route into a job.
explanation.walkthrough: POLLIN(G ST)ATION: a worker bee's job is pollination. In Britain schools are often used as places to vote on election day.
explanation.definitionFit: On election day many school halls serve as the places where people go to cast their votes.

indicators.note: rocks, as a verb, means shakes about, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of building materials: concrete and particular stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concrete' and 'rocks' suggest a building site, but 'Made concrete' means given bodily form.
explanation.definitionFit: To incarnate an idea is to embody it in flesh or real form, making something abstract tangible.

blocks.note: a log is a written record
a jam is an improvised jazz session

explanation.surface: A band breaks off to tape their improvised jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage that brings things to a halt, so it is a stop or stoppage.

clue.text: In truth, not entirely popular American politician

indicators.note: not entirely tells us the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: frankly means truthfully, in truth
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A US politician who is honestly not wholly liked.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Franklin was a Founding Father of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was a statesman who helped draft the Declaration of Independence and served as a diplomat.

indicators.note: something that grabs another holds it within its grip

blocks.note: a fish is a swimmer
a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A tired swimmer clutches a bar in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: F(RAIL)ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so the word means somewhat frail, which is rather weak.

indicators.note: something that houses another gives it a home inside itself

blocks.note: thy is the archaic form of your
under means down, below

explanation.surface: An instruction to shut down your former houses.
explanation.walkthrough: TH(UNDER)Y. 'Close' looks like the verb to shut; it is the adjective for humid weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is warm and oppressive, the heavy humid kind that comes before a storm.

indicators.note: sandwiches means the words hold the answer between them like a filling

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Look for the sandwiches near the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food on the menu, but it is the verb saying the words enclose the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or discover it, which means to find.

clue.text: Losing vote, fakes cheers for party

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the following word

blocks.note: a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper
to fix a result is to fake it
ta is British slang for thanks, cheers

explanation.surface: A party that lost the vote rigs it and celebrates anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'cheers' and 'ta' are both casual ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive celebration, especially in Spain, so it is a party.

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, Sunday
hi is a greeting
very means extremely

explanation.surface: The sun's warmth is welcome when it is bitterly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivery describes feeling chilly and inclined to shiver, so it means cold.

indicators.note: contains says the city name holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: Delhi is the Indian capital region
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: An Indian city has a peaceful refuge in it.
explanation.walkthrough: DEL(P)HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the ancient Greek sacred site of Apollo's oracle, a holy precinct or sanctuary.

clue.text: Very long joke in an idealess novel

indicators.note: in says the first piece sits inside the jumbled letters that follow
novel means new, so the letters before it are given a new order

blocks.note: a quip is a joke
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A long-winded joke appears in a novel with no ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer comes from Latin for a foot and a half long, applied to over-long words.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes long words, or a fondness for them, so it fits very long applied to words.

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for a house or flat; digs are lodgings
second meaning: a pole with a hook for landing large fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like a verb about excavating, but it is a noun for lodgings, and a gaff is British slang for one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a place where someone lives and a hooked stick used by anglers.

clue.text: A court case not quite enough for courts

indicators.note: not quite enough means falling a little short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a trial is a case heard in court

explanation.surface: A legal case with too little evidence for the courts to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' looks like law courts, but here it means courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court in a building, so the plural matches courts in the courtyard sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: a tool or means by which something is done
second meaning: to carry out a plan or policy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' suggests a spy being deployed; it is a noun for an instrument, and the second half is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a tool that acts on something and a verb for carrying a plan into effect.

clue.text: Physicist in the RAF worried about explosive

indicators.note: worried means agitated or shaken up, so the letters are scrambled
about says the jumbled letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A scientist serving in the air force is anxious about a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the jumbled letters, not just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit was the German physicist who devised the mercury thermometer and its temperature scale.

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: dry means dull or boring
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A composer's dull book has been turned down by publishers.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English Renaissance composer.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was a leading Tudor composer of church music and keyboard pieces.
